jobs.title: Data Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
**Company Overview**
--------------------

Verne is building physical AI to make physical work as scalable as software and bring general-purpose robots to every business. We develop robots, foundation models, and the tools that turn them into reliable industrial deployments.

Our open-weight world action model, Verne V0.5, brings together video and action learning. Alongside it, we build data and training systems, a fine-tuning platform, and inference and control software. Our work is grounded in real deployments: learning new tasks efficiently, adapting to different environments, and operating reliably in production.

**The Role**
------------

We’re looking for a Data Infrastructure Engineer to own and build the data systems that power Verne’s robots in the real world. This is a hands-on founding engineer role with true ownership and freedom — your work will directly impact robots performing customer-critical tasks every day.

You will architect and deploy data pipelines on both AWS and edge devices, manage large-scale multi-modal datasets (images, video, time-series, text, etc.), and build the tooling that connects real-world robot data to training and evaluation workflows. You’ll work across the full robotics software stack, from ingesting sensor data and telemetry, to enabling large-scale policy learning pipelines that drive production robots.

Beyond writing great code, you’ll help drive technical decisions, lead cross-functional efforts, and bridge robotics, machine learning, and product requirements into scalable, reliable systems.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* Build and own our data backbone on AWS: Design and run cloud + edge pipelines using services like IoT Core, S3, ECR, Batch, ECS/EKS, and Step Functions. Your work keeps robot data flowing reliably and cost-efficiently from the field into the lab.
* Develop on-device data systems: Build robust, fault-tolerant data capture on edge PCs using MCAP/Protobuf, with clean schema contracts, buffering, and resumable uploads to the cloud.
* Wrangle massive multimodal datasets: Organize and version millions of images, videos, time-series (robot state, force/torque), and annotations. Enforce metadata, retention, and access patterns that scale.
* Build MLOps and DataOps pipelines: Automate data validation, labeling, augmentation, and model training/evaluation using containerized jobs and orchestrators like Batch, Step Functions, Airflow, or Prefect.
* Ensure data quality and health: Create ingestion checks, schema validation, deduping, drift detection, and real-time alerting around data freshness and completeness.
* Build internal tools that unblock others: Develop UIs/CLIs for browsing data, launching jobs, tracking experiments, and debugging robots in the field. Integrate with tools like Foxglove.
* Work across teams: Partner with hardware, ML, and product to turn raw field data into smarter robots and real customer value—fast.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* B.S., M.S., Ph.D. in computer science or related fields.
* Strong programming skills in Python (you write clean, efficient, production-ready code)
* Strong experience in AWS
* Systems engineering skills (networking, concurrency, performance)
* At least 2 years of full-time work experience for candidates with a B.S. in related fields. 1 year of experience for M.S. or Ph.D. candidates.

**Why Join Us**
---------------

At Verne, you won’t just be writing code — you’ll be shaping the future of physical AI. Our mission is simple but ambitious: free humans from tedious manual work by deploying low-cost robotic automation at scale and democratizing bimanual robot manipulators for the world.

You’ll build systems that run on real robots, in real customer environments, driving immediate and tangible impact. You’ll join a small, world-class team where your ideas matter, your ownership is real, and your growth is accelerated. If you’re excited by hard problems, fast execution, and the chance to industrialize AI in the physical world, this is the team to be on.

**Details**
-----------

* Location: South San Francisco, CA (on-site required)
* Compensation: Competitive salary + meaningful equity
* Perks: Free meals vouchers, hardware access, health benefits, PTO

Compensation Range: $140K - $175K

jobs.description:

**The Role**
------------

We’re looking for a talented Software Engineer to design and build the core systems that power Verne’s robots in the real world. This is a hands-on role where your work will directly translate to physical robots performing customer-critical tasks. You’ll work across the full robotics software stack, from low-level sensor and actuator interfaces, to deploying large-scale policy learning pipelines, to shipping reliable features that customers depend on. Beyond just writing code, you’ll help design solutions, lead engineering efforts, and think cross-functionally to bridge hardware, machine learning, and product requirements.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* Build and optimize robotics software in Python and C++, spanning device drivers, control interfaces, and high-level APIs that power real-world deployments.
* Integrate and deploy ML policies (PyTorch) into visuomotor control loops, ensuring efficient inference on edge hardware.
* Design and test training pipelines for policy learning, including dataset preparation, augmentation, and scaling across massive multi-modal datasets (video, teleop trajectories, sensor streams).
* Develop infrastructure for teleoperation and autonomy, including real-time data streaming, low-latency WebRTC systems, and fallback human-in-the-loop control.
* Prototype new robot capabilities by collaborating closely with the hardware and research teams, translating experimental ideas into production-ready features.
* Systematically evaluate and test policies through lab trials and live customer proofs of concept, measuring performance, robustness, and safety at scale.
* Contribute to cloud + edge scaling efforts, including AWS-based data ingestion pipelines, IoT fleet management, and distributed training/serving infrastructure.
* Take ownership of engineering projects end-to-end, from design discussions and architecture, to implementation, testing, and deployment in the field.
* Work cross-functionally with product, research, and customer teams to ensure the systems you build align with real-world needs and unlock tangible customer value.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* B.S., M.S., Ph.D. in computer science or related fields.
* Strong programming skills in Python (you write clean, efficient, production-ready code)
* Solid experience with PyTorch and modern ML workflows
* Systems engineering skills (networking, concurrency, performance)
* At least 3 years of full-time work experience for candidates with a B.S. in related fields. 1 year of experience for M.S. or Ph.D. candidates.
* Experience with robotic arms, embedded systems, etc (e.g., Arduinos, motors, robot arms)

**Preferred**
-------------

* Experience with real-time systems (cameras, sensors, streaming)
* Hands-on with AWS services (EC2, IoT, WebRTC)

**Why Join Us**
---------------

At Verne, you won’t just be writing code, you’ll be shaping the future of physical AI. You’ll see your work run on real robots, in real customer environments, with immediate impact. You’ll join a small, world-class team where your contributions matter and your growth is accelerated.

**Details**
-----------

* Location: South San Francisco, CA (on-site required)
* Compensation: Competitive salary + meaningful equity
* Perks: Free meals vouchers, hardware access, health benefits, PTO

This is a rare chance to join a YC-backed robotics startup early and help build the foundation of the company. If you’re excited about robots, passionate about solving hard problems, and eager to see your work come alive in the real world — we’d love to hear from you.

Compensation Range: $140K - $200K

jobs.title: Robotics Software Engineer – Motion Planning
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

Premier Global Links LLC is seeking a talented **Robotics Software Engineer** for an innovative technology company developing advanced AI-powered robotics systems for life sciences and laboratory automation.

This role focuses on building software that enables robotic arms to operate scientific instruments with human-like precision and dexterity. You will work on motion planning, trajectory optimization, computer vision, and robotics software integration to help robots perform complex tasks in dynamic laboratory environments.

The ideal candidate has hands-on robotics software development experience, strong programming skills in C++ or Python, and an interest in deploying intelligent robotic systems on real-world hardware.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Develop and implement motion planning and trajectory optimization algorithms for robotic arm manipulators.
* Build software that enables robots to operate scientific instruments and laboratory equipment.
* Integrate, test, and debug robotics software across simulation environments and physical robots.
* Develop computer vision capabilities that allow robots to recognize, manipulate, and interact with laboratory tools and consumables.
* Implement collision avoidance and motion control solutions for dynamic laboratory environments.
* Work with simulation tools to develop, test, and validate robotic behaviors.
* Deploy and maintain robotics software running on physical hardware.
* Collaborate with scientists and technical teams at customer laboratories to understand operational challenges and develop practical solutions.
* Troubleshoot robotics software and hardware integration issues.
* Improve robotics platform scalability, reliability, performance, and robustness.
* Contribute to the development of software architecture and engineering best practices.

**Required Qualifications**

* 1–8 years of professional experience in robotics software engineering or a closely related technical field.
* Strong programming experience in **C++ or Python**.
* Understanding of robotics software development and robotic arm manipulators.
* Experience with motion planning, trajectory optimization, or robotic control systems.
* Ability to develop, test, and debug software for real-world robotic systems.
* Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
* Ability to collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering and scientific teams.
* Comfortable working in a fast-paced, on-site engineering environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with robotics simulation frameworks such as **PyBullet or MuJoCo**.
* Familiarity with computer vision and perception systems.
* Experience with collision detection and avoidance in robotic environments.
* Knowledge of robotics communication and infrastructure tools such as ZMQ, Redis, and gRPC.
* Experience integrating software with physical robots, sensors, and scientific instruments.
* Exposure to laboratory automation, life sciences, or scientific equipment.
* Experience deploying robotics applications in production or customer environments.

**Compensation & Equity**

* Annual base salary: **$148,000–$230,000**, depending on qualifications and experience.
* Competitive equity opportunity.
* Full-time employment.

**Work Location & Schedule**

* San Francisco, California.
* On-site position, five days per week.
* Candidates must be able to work from the San Francisco office.

**Work Authorization**

Eligible visa transfers and new visa sponsorships may be considered, including OPT, H-1B transfers, new H-1B sponsorship, and TN status, subject to applicable eligibility and employer requirements.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Premier Global Links LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to legally protected characteristics and in accordance with applicable employment laws.

* Experience designing and developing APIs and scalable software applications.
* Ability to contribute across the full software development lifecycle.
* Strong communication and collaboration skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience building and scaling products at a fast-growing technology company or startup.
* Familiarity with Flutter or cross-platform mobile application development.
* Experience with AWS and cloud-based application infrastructure.
* Exposure to AI-powered applications, LLMs, speech recognition, or audio processing.
* Experience with healthcare technology, clinical software, or Electronic Health Record (EHR) integrations.
* Experience with automated testing, CI/CD, and production deployment practices.

Eligible visa transfers may be considered, including OPT, H-1B transfers, and TN status, subject to applicable eligibility and employer requirements. New H-1B sponsorship is not currently available under the stated program. Green card sponsorship may be considered after six months, subject to approval.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Runtime Infrastructure
jobs.description:
New York, NY • Los Angeles, CA • Austin, TX • Seattle, WA

Software Engineering

In office

Full-time

**About Nominal**
-----------------

Engineers today are building some of the most ambitious machines humanity has ever seen. They should have AI that’s purpose-built for them.

  
  

Nominal is building the Hardware Intelligence Platform that gives engineers increased visibility into complex physical systems, helps them make better decisions, and ultimately gets their products into the real world faster. It brings together the systems, data, intelligence, and applications hardware engineering requires to meet the AI moment. Hardware engineering teams use Nominal to simulate, test, manufacture, and operate the physical systems that keep the world moving, from spacecraft and autonomous vehicles to next-generation energy systems and robotics.

  
  

Our customers span aerospace, defense, manufacturing, transportation, energy, and robotics. They include Anduril, Shield AI, Wisk Aero, Pratt Miller Motorsports, Antares, and Shinkei Systems, amongst others, alongside programs within the U.S. Air Force and Navy. Our team draws from SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Applied Intuition, Tesla, and other leading companies, united by a common mission: giving hardware engineers the tools to build the future with speed, safety, and confidence. We're a fast-moving team that owns problems end-to-end, works across disciplines, and thrives at the intersection of hardware and software.

  
  

Some of the world’s leading technology investors, including Sequoia, Lightspeed, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Lux Capital, and Insight Partners, are backing Nominal’s ambition to change how machines are built and operated. We’re looking for engineers who want to take on hard problems and help make a new generation of world-changing hardware possible.

  
  

### **Join Nominal as a Software Engineer, Runtime Infrastructure**

Nominal runs mission-critical software wherever our customers need it: in our cloud, in theirs, and on disconnected networks for defense programs. An engineer might be watching a vehicle in real time or working through terabytes of post-test data. Either way, every layer between the hardware and the chart on their screen has to be fast and correct. Our customers expect a lot from us on reliability, security, and compliance. Runtime Infrastructure builds the libraries, services, and standards that let every Nominal team meet that bar by default.

  
  

As a Software Engineer on Runtime Infrastructure, you'll build the foundation the rest of engineering builds on. That covers how our services and applications are observed, how they record who did what, how they talk to each other, and how they behave under load and failure. Your main users are other Nominal engineers. If you do this well, they ship faster, catch problems sooner, and meet our customers' standards without having to think about it. Through them, your work reaches the aerospace, defense, and autonomy teams who use Nominal for mission-critical testing.

  
  

We're hiring both backend and full stack engineers for this team. You'll build services, libraries, and APIs that have to be correct, fast, and long-lived. You'll care about architecture across the whole stack: how our web applications are structured, how they talk to the backend, and how they behave in production. You'll have a lot of autonomy and work closely with product, frontend, platform, and deployment engineers. You'll help shape the requirements yourself, with input from fellow engineers and our customers, and make the tradeoffs that decide how our systems are built. You'll also be able to contribute to the open source projects we depend on.

  
  

### **About the role**

**Build the foundation other engineers stand on**

Build the service frameworks and shared libraries that every Nominal service starts from: configuration, health checks, graceful shutdown, resource limits, resilience, secure defaults, and the conventions for how services define their APIs and talk to each other. The goal is that a new service is reliable, observable, and compliant from its first commit. You'll measure success by how quickly other engineers can ship, debug, and operate their own services.

  
  

**Find where the time and memory go**

Investigate concurrency, memory, and latency problems across our services. You'll build runtime metrics, profiling, and load testing, then turn what you find into fixes, and into tools other engineers can use on their own.

  
  

**Success in this role comes from treating other engineers as your customers. You'll spend as much time understanding how teams build, run, and debug software as you will writing code.**

  

### **We'd love to hear from you if you have**

* 3+ years of experience as a backend or full stack engineer, building and running production systems where performance, reliability, and operational simplicity matter.
* Strong experience in at least one of Rust, Java, or TypeScript, with an emphasis on correctness, clarity, and long-lived systems. You don't need all three, but you should be excited to work across them.
* Experience designing libraries, frameworks, or APIs that other engineers build on: hiding complexity behind simple interfaces, sensible defaults, and changing things without breaking the people who depend on you.
* Hands-on experience with observability tools such as OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, or Datadog, including metrics, traces, and alerts that engineers actually rely on.
* A solid understanding of concurrency, async runtimes, networking, and how distributed systems behave under load and failure.
* A systems mindset. You like working out how a system should behave, and how it will fail, before you build it.
* Excellent communication skills, and the ability to explain technical tradeoffs clearly to the engineers who depend on your work.
* A bias toward ownership: you design it, build it, ship it, and run it.

### **Join Nominal as a Full Stack Software Engineer, Compute**

At Nominal, the frontend goes far beyond a visual layer on top of APIs. It's where thousands of high-frequency data sources are streamed and drawn on screen in time for an engineer to decide whether to continue, pause, or abort tests running against real hardware. Our customers monitor mission-critical systems through Nominal, so the data has to be fast, correct, and trustworthy at every layer. Meeting that bar means balancing raw performance with an experience engineers can depend on and understand, so they can build trust in the platform.

  
  

We're looking for product engineers who care about high-scale data computation, runtime performance, and device constraints as much as building intuitive interfaces. You'll work at the intersection of product, design, and engineering to turn a highly expressive compute engine into the foundation that every visualization in Nominal depends on, from highly optimized time series charts to flexible user-defined custom visualizations. Success in this role is measured by building a data layer that stays fast, correct, and observable on whatever device and network our customers bring.

  
  

You'll partner closely with backend engineers, designers, and product teams to define workflows, shape product direction, and make thoughtful technical tradeoffs in an environment where requirements are often ambiguous and the best solutions aren't immediately obvious. You'll own the shared compute and data layer of the platform’s applications end to end. Your judgment will shape how live and historical data workflows feel across the whole product.

  
  

### **About the role**

**Build the data foundation every application stands on**

Own the layer between Nominal's compute engine and the user: streaming over WebSockets, orchestrating web workers, handling columnar data formats, caching intelligently, and processing live and historical data on the client. You'll design generalized data and compute capabilities that serve today's product and the use cases we haven't met yet, so that new panels, new query types, and open-ended user-defined visualizations can be built quickly on the stability and guarantees already in place.

  
  

**Make performance and correctness non-negotiable**

Customers stream thousands of high-frequency series into live monitoring dashboards with low-latency expectations and zero tolerance for incorrect data. You'll squeeze everything possible out of varied user hardware, hunt memory leaks down to the allocation, benchmark and profile the render pipeline, and handle out-of-order, late, and missing data so the picture on screen converges on the truth.

  
  

**Own ambiguous product problems**

Partner closely with product, design, and engineering to turn loosely defined ideas into intuitive user experiences. You'll challenge assumptions, validate workflows directly with users, and make confident product decisions when requirements are incomplete.

  
  

**Bring new compute capabilities to users**

Take new features from the compute layer and expose them in a composable, scalable form that end users can understand: new capabilities, aggregations, grouping mechanisms, and transforms that can power every application and workflow in the Nominal platform.

  
  

**Make complexity feel simple**

Design experiences that expose powerful capabilities without overwhelming users. You'll think deeply about information architecture, interaction design, and how technical users reason about their work.

  
  

**Success in this role comes from combining strong frontend engineering with product judgment. You'll spend as much time thinking about how users reason about complex systems as you will writing React code.**

**About Nominal**
-----------------

Engineers today are building some of the most ambitious machines humanity has ever seen. They should have AI that’s purpose-built for them.

  
  

Nominal is building the Hardware Intelligence Platform that gives engineers increased visibility into complex physical systems, helps them make better decisions, and ultimately gets their products into the real world faster. It brings together the systems, data, intelligence, and applications hardware engineering requires to meet the AI moment. Hardware engineering teams use Nominal to simulate, test, manufacture, and operate the physical systems that keep the world moving, from spacecraft and autonomous vehicles to next-generation energy systems and robotics.

  
  

Our customers span aerospace, defense, manufacturing, transportation, energy, and robotics. They include Anduril, Shield AI, Wisk Aero, Pratt Miller Motorsports, Antares, and Shinkei Systems, amongst others, alongside programs within the U.S. Air Force and Navy. Our team draws from SpaceX, Palantir, Anduril, Applied Intuition, Tesla, and other leading companies, united by a common mission: giving hardware engineers the tools to build the future with speed, safety, and confidence. We're a fast-moving team that owns problems end-to-end, works across disciplines, and thrives at the intersection of hardware and software.

  
  

Some of the world’s leading technology investors, including Sequoia, Lightspeed, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Lux Capital, and Insight Partners, are backing Nominal’s ambition to change how machines are built and operated. We’re looking for engineers who want to take on hard problems and help make a new generation of world-changing hardware possible.

  
  

### **Join Nominal as a Software Engineer, Runtime Infrastructure**

Nominal runs mission-critical software wherever our customers need it: in our cloud, in theirs, and on disconnected networks for defense programs. An engineer might be watching a vehicle in real time or working through terabytes of post-test data. Either way, every layer between the hardware and the chart on their screen has to be fast and correct. Our customers expect a lot from us on reliability, security, and compliance. Runtime Infrastructure builds the libraries, services, and standards that let every Nominal team meet that bar by default.

  
  

As a Software Engineer on Runtime Infrastructure, you'll build the foundation the rest of engineering builds on. That covers how our services and applications are observed, how they record who did what, how they talk to each other, and how they behave under load and failure. Your main users are other Nominal engineers. If you do this well, they ship faster, catch problems sooner, and meet our customers' standards without having to think about it. Through them, your work reaches the aerospace, defense, and autonomy teams who use Nominal for mission-critical testing.

  
  

We're hiring both backend and full stack engineers for this team. You'll build services, libraries, and APIs that have to be correct, fast, and long-lived. You'll care about architecture across the whole stack: how our web applications are structured, how they talk to the backend, and how they behave in production. You'll have a lot of autonomy and work closely with product, frontend, platform, and deployment engineers. You'll help shape the requirements yourself, with input from fellow engineers and our customers, and make the tradeoffs that decide how our systems are built. You'll also be able to contribute to the open source projects we depend on.

  
  

### **About the role**

**Build the foundation other engineers stand on**

Build the service frameworks and shared libraries that every Nominal service starts from: configuration, health checks, graceful shutdown, resource limits, resilience, secure defaults, and the conventions for how services define their APIs and talk to each other. The goal is that a new service is reliable, observable, and compliant from its first commit. You'll measure success by how quickly other engineers can ship, debug, and operate their own services.

  
  

**Find where the time and memory go**

Investigate concurrency, memory, and latency problems across our services. You'll build runtime metrics, profiling, and load testing, then turn what you find into fixes, and into tools other engineers can use on their own.

  
  

**Success in this role comes from treating other engineers as your customers. You'll spend as much time understanding how teams build, run, and debug software as you will writing code.**

  

### **We'd love to hear from you if you have**

* 3+ years of experience as a backend or full stack engineer, building and running production systems where performance, reliability, and operational simplicity matter.
* Strong experience in at least one of Rust, Java, or TypeScript, with an emphasis on correctness, clarity, and long-lived systems. You don't need all three, but you should be excited to work across them.
* Experience designing libraries, frameworks, or APIs that other engineers build on: hiding complexity behind simple interfaces, sensible defaults, and changing things without breaking the people who depend on you.
* Hands-on experience with observability tools such as OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, or Datadog, including metrics, traces, and alerts that engineers actually rely on.
* A solid understanding of concurrency, async runtimes, networking, and how distributed systems behave under load and failure.
* A systems mindset. You like working out how a system should behave, and how it will fail, before you build it.
* Excellent communication skills, and the ability to explain technical tradeoffs clearly to the engineers who depend on your work.
* A bias toward ownership: you design it, build it, ship it, and run it.

Meeting that bar means balancing raw performance with an experience engineers can depend on and understand, so they can build trust in the platform.

You'll work at the intersection of product, design, and engineering to turn a highly expressive compute engine into the foundation that every visualization in Nominal depends on, from highly optimized time series charts to flexible user-defined custom visualizations. Success in this role is measured by building a data layer that stays fast, correct, and observable on whatever device and network our customers bring.

  
  

You'll partner closely with backend engineers, designers, and product teams to define workflows, shape product direction, and make thoughtful technical tradeoffs in an environment where requirements are often ambiguous and the best solutions aren't immediately obvious. You'll own the shared compute and data layer of the platform’s applications end to end. Your judgment will shape how live and historical data workflows feel across the whole product.

**Build the data foundation every application stands on**

Own the layer between Nominal's compute engine and the user: streaming over WebSockets, orchestrating web workers, handling columnar data formats, caching intelligently, and processing live and historical data on the client. You'll design generalized data and compute capabilities that serve today's product and the use cases we haven't met yet, so that new panels, new query types, and open-ended user-defined visualizations can be built quickly on the stability and guarantees already in place.

  
  

**Make performance and correctness non-negotiable**

Customers stream thousands of high-frequency series into live monitoring dashboards with low-latency expectations and zero tolerance for incorrect data. You'll squeeze everything possible out of varied user hardware, hunt memory leaks down to the allocation, benchmark and profile the render pipeline, and handle out-of-order, late, and missing data so the picture on screen converges on the truth.

Partner closely with product, design, and engineering to turn loosely defined ideas into intuitive user experiences. You'll challenge assumptions, validate workflows directly with users, and make confident product decisions when requirements are incomplete.

Take new features from the compute layer and expose them in a composable, scalable form that end users can understand: new capabilities, aggregations, grouping mechanisms, and transforms that can power every application and workflow in the Nominal platform.

Design experiences that expose powerful capabilities without overwhelming users. You'll think deeply about information architecture, interaction design, and how technical users reason about their work.
